metadata.methodology: Symptoms extracted only when explicitly mentioned by at least 2 authoritative medical sources. Synonyms normalized. False negatives preferred over false positives.

diseases.description: A condition in which the blood vessels have persistently raised pressure. Often asymptomatic, but can lead to severe health complications like heart disease and stroke.
diseases.etiology: Primary (essential) is multifactorial; Secondary is caused by underlying conditions like kidney disease

diseases.description: A condition where the major blood vessels that supply the heart (coronary arteries) struggle to send enough blood, oxygen and nutrients to the heart muscle, usually due to plaque buildup.
diseases.etiology: Atherosclerosis (plaque buildup) in the coronary arteries

symptoms.symptom_name: pain radiating to arms, shoulders, or jaw

diseases.description: Chest pain or discomfort that typically occurs with activity or stress, resulting from poor blood flow through the blood vessels in the heart.
diseases.etiology: Reduced blood flow to the heart muscle, usually due to coronary artery disease

symptoms.symptom_name: pain spreading to arms, neck, jaw, or back

diseases.description: A serious medical emergency in which the supply of blood to the heart is suddenly blocked, usually by a blood clot, leading to heart muscle damage.
diseases.etiology: Complete blockage of a coronary artery, often from a ruptured plaque

symptoms.symptom_name: chest pain or discomfort (often described as pressure or squeezing)
pain radiating to arm, back, neck, or jaw

diseases.description: A long-term condition where the heart is unable to pump blood around the body properly.
diseases.etiology: Coronary heart disease, high blood pressure, cardiomyopathy, or heart valve problems

symptoms.symptom_name: shortness of breath (especially with activity or when lying down)
swelling in legs, ankles, or feet
sudden weight gain from fluid retention

diseases.description: A heart condition that causes an irregular and often abnormally fast heart rate, increasing the risk of stroke and heart failure.
diseases.etiology: Abnormal electrical impulses in the atria of the heart

diseases.description: An abnormally fast heartbeat that starts in the upper chambers of the heart (atria), causing the heart to beat faster than normal, often in sudden episodes.
diseases.etiology: Faulty electrical connections in the heart

diseases.description: A heart rate that is too slow, generally defined as less than 60 beats per minute, which can prevent the brain and other organs from getting enough oxygen.
diseases.etiology: Damage to heart tissue, medications (e.g., beta blockers), hypothyroidism, or sick sinus syndrome

diseases.description: A common condition where a build-up of fatty deposits in the arteries restricts blood supply to leg muscles.
diseases.etiology: Atherosclerosis in peripheral arteries

symptoms.symptom_name: leg pain or cramping when walking
numbness or weakness in the legs
coldness in lower leg or foot
sores on toes or feet that won't heal
changes in skin color of legs
hair loss or slower hair growth on legs

diseases.description: A general term for diseases of the heart muscle, where the walls of the heart chambers have become stretched, thickened, or stiff, reducing its ability to pump blood.
diseases.etiology: Genetic mutations, chronic high blood pressure, prior heart attacks, infections, or excessive alcohol use

symptoms.symptom_name: swelling in legs, ankles, and feet

diseases.description: Damage or defect in one or more of the four heart valves, preventing them from opening or closing properly.
diseases.etiology: Congenital defects, aging, rheumatic fever, infections, or other heart conditions

diseases.description: A condition in which the two valve flaps of the mitral valve do not close smoothly or evenly, but instead bulge (prolapse) upward into the left atrium.
diseases.etiology: Often genetic or related to connective tissue disorders

diseases.description: Narrowing of the aortic valve opening, which restricts the blood flow from the left ventricle to the aorta and may also affect the pressure in the left atrium.
diseases.etiology: Age-related calcification, congenital bicuspid valve, or rheumatic fever

diseases.description: A condition in which the aortic valve does not close tightly, allowing blood to flow backward from the aorta into the left ventricle.
diseases.etiology: Congenital heart defects, infective endocarditis, rheumatic fever, or aortic dissection

symptoms.symptom_name: shortness of breath (especially with exertion or when lying down)

diseases.description: A condition in which the mitral valve does not close tightly, allowing blood to flow backward into the left atrium.
diseases.etiology: Mitral valve prolapse, rheumatic heart disease, endocarditis, or heart attack

symptoms.symptom_name: shortness of breath (especially with exertion or when lying down)

diseases.description: Inflammation of the pericardium, the thin, sac-like membrane surrounding the heart.
diseases.etiology: Viral infections (most common), heart attack, systemic inflammatory disorders, or trauma

symptoms.symptom_name: sharp chest pain (worsens with deep breathing or lying down, improves when sitting up and leaning forward)

diseases.description: Inflammation of the heart muscle (myocardium), which can reduce the heart's ability to pump and cause rapid or abnormal heart rhythms.
diseases.etiology: Viral infections (most common), bacterial/parasitic infections, or autoimmune reactions
risk_factors: exposure to certain chemicals or medications

symptoms.symptom_name: swelling of the legs, ankles, and feet

diseases.description: An infection of the endocardium, the inner lining of your heart chambers and heart valves.
diseases.etiology: Bacteria or fungi entering the bloodstream and attaching to abnormal areas of the heart

diseases.description: A condition that occurs when a blood clot forms in a deep vein, usually in the legs, which can lead to a pulmonary embolism if it breaks loose.
diseases.etiology: Blood pooling in deep veins causing clot formation, often due to immobility or hypercoagulability

symptoms.symptom_name: pain or tenderness in the leg (often starting in the calf)
red or discolored skin on the leg
warm skin in the affected area

diseases.description: A condition caused by excess fluid in the lungs, making it difficult to breathe. Most commonly caused by heart problems (cardiogenic pulmonary edema).
diseases.etiology: Heart failure (cardiogenic) or direct lung damage/ARDS (noncardiogenic)

symptoms.symptom_name: cough that produces frothy sputum (may be blood-tinged)
anxiety, restlessness or a feeling of apprehension

diseases.description: One or more abnormalities in the heart's structure that are present at birth, affecting how blood flows through the heart and out to the rest of the body.
diseases.etiology: Developmental defects during pregnancy, often genetic or chromosomal
risk_factors: maternal diabetes or rubella during pregnancy

symptoms.symptom_name: rapid breathing or shortness of breath
poor weight gain or feeding difficulties

diseases.description: A small hole between the two upper chambers of the heart (atria) that didn't close naturally after birth as it should.
diseases.etiology: Failure of the normal fetal opening between atria to close after birth

diseases.description: A common heart defect present at birth consisting of a hole in the wall (septum) that separates the two lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart.
diseases.etiology: Congenital defect

symptoms.symptom_name: shortness of breath or rapid breathing
poor feeding and failure to thrive

diseases.description: A disease in which the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick (hypertrophied), making it harder for the heart to pump blood.
diseases.etiology: Often caused by abnormal genes (mutations) in the heart muscle

diseases.description: A sudden, unexpected loss of heart function, breathing, and consciousness, usually resulting from an electrical disturbance in the heart.
diseases.etiology: Ventricular fibrillation, heart attack, severe trauma, or profound electrolyte imbalances
risk_factors: family history of sudden cardiac arrest
